Angioleiomyoma: smooth muscle and vascular channels on histopathology
Microscopic examination showed thick bands of smooth muscle staining positive for smooth muscle antigens using immunochemistry
Selective superior mesenteric angiography showed a large hyper vascular mass near the terminal ileum in the right iliac fossa
Smooth muscle appeared to arise from the muscularis propria of the small bowel
Histopathology of the resected tumor showed a submucosal tumor compressing the mucosal lining causing ulceration
Sectional analysis of the tumour showed thick bands of muscle with vascular spongy stroma
No significant mitotic activity in the tumor and no evidence of tumor necrosis

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with angioleiomyoma, which is characterized by intermittent gastrointestinal bleeding, melena, light-headedness, anemia, and a hypervascular mass on angiography. The histopathology of the resected tumor also showed a submucosal tumor compressing the mucosal lining causing ulceration, with thick bands of smooth muscle and vascular channels.

While leiomyoma can cause gastrointestinal bleeding and abdominal pain, the patient's symptoms and laboratory results are more consistent with angioleiomyoma. However, leiomyoma is still a possible diagnosis, as it can present with a mass on imaging and smooth muscle on histopathology.
